_comment: Where each animated explainer is injected. Keyed by output page slug. 'afterSection' is the GitHub anchor slug of the H2 section the figure is appended to; the markdown is never edited. If afterSection does not match a real section the build fails loudly rather than silently dropping the animation. 'title' is plain text and is HTML-escaped by the build, so write literal characters (> not >); 'caption' is injected as HTML so it may contain tags such as <code>.

05-consistent-hashing.title: Try it: how many keys actually move?
05-consistent-hashing.caption: Add and remove servers and watch the share of keys that get remapped. Switch between plain hash(key) % N and the hash ring to see the difference the chapter is describing.

04-rate-limiter.title: Try it: the five algorithms on one traffic stream
04-rate-limiter.caption: Every panel sees exactly the same requests. Send a steady trickle, then a burst, then a burst that straddles a window boundary, and watch where each algorithm accepts and where it rejects.

06-key-value-store.title: Try it: why W + R > N is the whole rule
06-key-value-store.caption: Move the sliders and watch the write set and the read set overlap — or come apart. The guarantee is pigeonhole, not magic.

07-unique-id-generator.title: Try it: spend the 64 bits yourself
07-unique-id-generator.caption: Every bit you give one field is taken from another. Change the split and see what it costs you in epoch length, machine count and IDs per millisecond.

11-news-feed-system.title: Try it: fan-out on write vs on read
11-news-feed-system.caption: Post as an ordinary user, then as the pop star, under each strategy. The same total work lands on opposite sides of the system — and one of the two sides falls over.

13-search-autocomplete.title: Try it: the walk is cheap, the ranking is not
13-search-autocomplete.caption: Type a prefix and watch where the work actually goes. Then turn on the cached top-k and watch the subtree scan disappear.

16-proximity-service.title: Try it: geohash precision and the boundary problem
16-proximity-service.caption: Drag the two pins. A shared prefix means a shared cell — but two points a metre apart can share no prefix at all, which is why neighbour cells have to be queried too.

21-ad-click-event-aggregation.title: Try it: event time, watermarks and late events
21-ad-click-event-aggregation.caption: Every event has a time it happened and a later time it arrived. Move the watermark lag and watch the trade between completeness and latency play out.

25-real-time-gaming-leaderboard.title: Try it: how a skip list finds a score
25-real-time-gaming-leaderboard.caption: Search runs along the sparse upper lanes and drops a level whenever the next hop would overshoot. That is the whole algorithm behind a Redis sorted set.

19-distributed-message-queue.title: Try it: partitions are the ceiling on parallelism
19-distributed-message-queue.caption: Add consumers past the partition count and watch them go idle. A partition goes to at most one consumer in a group, so the topic's partition count caps how fast the group can ever read.

24-s3-like-object-storage.title: Try it: erasure coding against replication
24-s3-like-object-storage.caption: Click a node to kill it. Any k of the k+m shards rebuild the object, so the same durability costs far less storage than three full copies — until you look at what a repair has to read.

27-digital-wallet.title: Try it: 2PC, TCC and Saga under the same failure
27-digital-wallet.caption: All three look identical when nothing goes wrong. Inject a failure at each step and watch them diverge — blocked locks, cancelled reservations, or compensation for something everyone has already seen.

28-stock-exchange.title: Try it: price-time priority is the whole matching rule
28-stock-exchange.caption: Send orders into the book. Anything priced across the spread trades immediately against the best resting order, oldest first; the remainder rests and becomes the new best price.
